newsitem.title: USA: Dade Cty, Fla., approves park bonds. [CORRECTED 18:56 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Dade Cty, Fla., approves park bonds. [CORRECTED 18:56 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline and text to make clear that voters voted to allow the arena to be built)

Voters in Dade County, Fla., approved a $200 million general obligation bond issue for public parks and agreed that the Miami Heat could build a new basketball stadium on public bayfront parkland, elections officials said.
The park bond passed with 311,946 yes votes, or 66.99 percent, and 153,725 no votes, or 33.01 percent.

The bond issue will raise $88 million for neighborhood parks, $77 million for regional parks, $12 million for MetroZoo, $4 million for Fairchild Tropical Gardens and $4 million for the county purchase of Parrot Jungle land.
The remaining $15 million would be used for beach renourishment projects.
Voters rejected proposal that would have prohibited the Heat from building a $165 million arena on public land adjacent to the Port of Miami.
The arena is to be built with private team money, though taxpayers will contribute $6.5 million a year for operating costs.

The block-the-arena proposal failed with 289,659 no votes or 58.94 percent, and 201,761 yes votes, or 41.06 percent. Because of the wording of the ballot language, voters who approve the project voted "no" and those opposing it voted "yes."
In a non-binding referendum, Dade voters approved a revenue sharing plan aimed at subsidizing basic services to poor municipalities.

The plan would allow the county to take control of up to three mills, or 30 percent, of the property taxes levied by each city. The revenues would go into a trust fund to be redistributed according to population, with wealthier cities receiving back less than they put in and poor communities receiving more.
But most voters ignored the straw ballot proposal, which received little attention proior to Tuesday's election. It passed with 1,121 yes votes, or 64.20 percent, and 625 no votes, or 35.8 percent.
